changed.where: Instead of blame, P1
changed.before: Be aware of what you are teaching your other positions. For example, are you teaching your little one that you are going to love them no matter what? Is it two separate positions, one making the vow to love your little one no matter what, and the other blaming your little one for not taking in your love? Or is it one position doing both of these things? Or are you blending them? Their age might not be your chronological age. Both talk in your grown-up voice, so to your little one they're the same. Be careful not to take the blaming as proof your love really is conditional, when it could just be another part talking.

changed.where: Appendix C: The extended de-hypnosis checklist, P3
changed.before: Before you do what it wants you to do, see if it does any of the following: create a sense of urgency, secrecy, shame, threat of exclusion if you don’t do what it says, specialness, sexual charge, spiritual superiority, ask you for money, ask you for sex, ask you for loyalty, ask you to be quiet, ask you to obey it, try to limit your choices, make it seem like it’s bad to question it, act like not obeying it is a problem that needs to be solved, make normal life seem boring/stupid/irrelevant in its presence, try to seduce/scare/rescue your inner child, not let your adult self say no.
changed.after:
Before you do what it wants you to do, check how it’s trying to get you there. Is it rushing you, or telling you to keep things secret? Is it shaming you, or threatening to leave you out if you don’t do what it says? Maybe it makes you feel special, or there’s a sexual charge to it, or a sense that you’re spiritually above everyone else.

Then look at what it wants from you. Is it money, or sex? Your loyalty? Is it asking you to keep quiet, or to obey it?

Keep in mind though, people who mean well can ask for some of these too. A teacher charges for their time, and your partner probably wants your loyalty. If you can say no to them and they’re fine with it, that’s a good sign.

Back to the interrogation:

Is it trying to narrow down your choices? Does questioning it feel like you’re doing something wrong, or does it act like not obeying is a problem you need to fix? Does normal life start to seem boring, stupid or irrelevant when it’s around? Is it trying to seduce, scare or rescue your inner child? And does it try to stop your adult self from saying no?
